results.claim: The rumble is just gas and fluid sliding through your intestines as they contract.
results.evidence: “produced by movement of the contents of the gastrointestinal tract… as they are propelled… by peristalsis… fluid and gas move forward in the intestines.”

results.claim: Peristalsis pushes the mixture along, and the moving gas creates the gurgle.
results.evidence: Source describes peristaltic muscle contractions moving contents, and gas moving produces the sound.

results.claim: When the stomach is empty, the space amplifies the noise, so growls are louder.
results.evidence: “The sound of air moving around the lumen of the stomach is amplified by the empty space.”

results.claim: You hear it strongest right before a meal.
results.evidence: “Louder rumbles may occur when the individual is hungry… before a meal.”

results.claim: Every 90 to 230 minutes, a fasting wave called the migrating motor complex sweeps the gut, creating the classic rumble.
results.evidence: MMC occurs every 90–230 minutes during the interdigestive phase and is responsible for the rumbling experienced when hungry.

results.claim: It also helps clear leftover food and bacteria between meals.
results.evidence: MMC acts as an “interdigestive housekeeper,” transporting indigestible substances and bacteria from the small intestine.

results.claim: Swallowed air while talking or drinking makes bubbles that add to the rumble.
results.evidence: “Stomach rumbles may also occur… when air is swallowed while talking, eating, and drinking.”

results.claim: Carbonated drinks can make the effect even louder.
results.evidence: “Stomach rumbles may also occur due to carbon dioxide moving through… following the consumption of carbonated drinks.”
